gap: Give the landscape continuous, grounded natural depth: smooth terrain materials and contour silhouettes with near/mid/far ridge separation and atmospheric falloff. The current faceted clumps and hard polygon verge remain the dominant mismatch in every view.
secondary_gaps: Golden hour is pale and low-contrast rather than the bar's saturated warm fields with coherent long shadows.
Night has stars and a readable ribbon, but little headlight pool or blue moonlit terrain separation compared with the bar.
Winter communicates a palette shift but leaves exposed polygon shoulders and patchy ground instead of continuous snow relief.
Cockpit geometry is recognizable yet lacks the bar's believable A-pillar/mirror framing and restrained dashboard proportions.
The elevated vista has a road and bridge but not the bar's broad water-backed composition and layered ridge depth.

evidence.note: Bar's rolling lake-backed hills, continuous grass and authored car read as a finished landscape; ours has a legible road and denser foliage but conspicuous faceted crowns, repeated clumps and flat pale verge.
Bar wins with saturated amber fields, controlled low sun and long shadows. Ours is washed toward the sun, with gray-green ground and weak shadow structure despite a readable chase car.
Ours supplies stars, tail lights and a visible road, but most terrain collapses to near-black. Bar retains a readable shoreline/mountain silhouette, blue night ramp and strong headlight cone.
Bar has a credible mirror, A-pillar, road and hillside under flat cloud light. Ours establishes a cockpit but the dark slab dashboard fills the lower frame and autumn vegetation is visibly faceted.
Bar is a coherent snow world with snow-shaped relief and integrated guardrail. Ours changes trees and ground toward white but leaves exposed tan polygon shoulder patches and a normal dark road.

Bar's elevated coastal frame has smooth cut slope, water and multiple atmospheric ridge layers. Ours has a readable elevated road/bridge but is a close, flat green patchwork with no water or comparable depth.

Bar's driver view is restrained and photographic with mirror, A-pillar and road cut. Ours has a centered road and detailed wheel, but noisy dark interior, oversized dash and low-poly verge are unmistakable.

verdict_text: Independent round-12 seven-shot blind review: the official bar wins all seven comparisons and the randomized side call is correct 7/7. The terrain shader pass improves contour variation and far bands, but the global read is still procedural low-poly scenery: hard-edged ground patches and repeated card foliage erase the continuous landform depth of the reference.
